context.analysis:
## Overview
This system gradually replaces a 30-year-old COBOL/DB2 mainframe claims system with a modern hybrid cloud platform. It enables online claim submissions and adjuster processing while maintaining the legacy mainframe as the system of record.

## Key Elements
* Customers and Brokers: External users submitting claims online
* Claims Adjusters: Internal users managing claims in the new web application
* IT Administrators: Internal staff managing operational tooling, feature flags, and rollbacks
* Modern Claims Platform: Azure-hosted web application and CQRS read/write services
* Legacy System: On-premise COBOL/DB2 mainframe claims system

## Relationships
* Customers/Brokers interact with Modern Claims Platform via HTTPS (REST API)
* Claims Adjusters interact with Modern Claims Platform via HTTPS (OAuth 2.0 / OIDC)
* Modern Claims Platform communicates with Legacy System via mTLS and asynchronous messaging
* Modern Claims Platform integrates with Azure Active Directory (Entra ID) for SSO

## Technology Stack
* Cloud Provider: Hybrid architecture utilizing Azure West Europe and on-premise mainframe
* Integration & Messaging: Azure Service Bus with idempotent consumers and circuit breakers
* Security: Azure Key Vault for secrets management and AES-256 encryption
* Observability: Azure App Insights, Managed Grafana, and Prometheus for centralized monitoring
* Configuration: Azure App Configuration for feature flagging and schema versioning

## Rationale
The hybrid architecture protects business continuity by keeping the mainframe as the system of record during the three-year migration. CQRS and asynchronous messaging isolate the modern UI from mainframe latency to ensure sub-two-second response times.

containers.analysis:
## Overview
The system is a hybrid modern claims platform that gradually replaces a 30-year-old COBOL/DB2 mainframe claims system while maintaining uninterrupted processing. It enables online claim submission for customers and a high-performance web interface for adjusters during a phased migration.

## Key Elements
- **Users:** Customers, Brokers, Claims Adjusters, Business Operations / Compliance Officers, IT Administrators.
- **Frontend Containers:** Customer Portal, Adjuster Web Application, Backend-For-Frontend (BFF) Container.
- **Integration & Core Containers:** Routing Container, Azure Service Bus, ArgoCD (GitOps).
- **External Systems:** COBOL/DB2 Mainframe (on-premises system of record), Azure Active Directory / Entra ID, Azure Key Vault.

## Relationships
- **Users to Frontend:** Customers/Brokers access the Customer Portal via HTTPS/TLS 1.3; Adjusters access the Adjuster Web Application using OAuth2/OIDC Single Sign-On authenticated against Azure AD.
- **Frontend to BFF:** Adjuster Web Application communicates with the BFF container via REST/HTTPS using OAuth2 Token Exchange (RFC 8693).
- **Platform to Mainframe:** Routing Container and BFF interact with the on-prem COBOL/DB2 Mainframe across a hybrid boundary secured by mTLS and circuit breakers.
- **Internal Messaging:** Containers exchange asynchronous events via Azure Service Bus with idempotent event publishing.

## Technology Stack
- **Cloud & Orchestration:** Hybrid deployment across On-Premises Mainframe and Azure West Europe using GitOps (ArgoCD) to standardize container rollouts and enable 1-day rollbacks.
- **Security & Identity:** Azure AD (Entra ID) for SSO/RBAC, Azure Key Vault with Managed Identities for secret management, and TLS 1.3 / mTLS for transport security.
- **Integration & Messaging:** Azure Service Bus for asynchronous message queuing and idempotent event publishing.
- **Observability:** OpenTelemetry for distributed tracing across Azure containers and the on-prem mainframe.

## Rationale
This hybrid architecture isolates incremental claim migrations while protecting the legacy mainframe during its 3-year phased retirement. The BFF caching layer and asynchronous messaging ensure adjuster UI performance targets are met despite slow legacy response times.

Customer Portal.analysis:
## Overview
The Insurance Claims Modernization system gradually replaces a 30-year-old mainframe claims platform with a hybrid cloud architecture in Azure West Europe while preserving legacy operations. It provides modern digital experiences for customers and brokers while maintaining strict data consistency and zero-downtime routing.

## Key Elements
* Customers and Brokers (Users)
* Claims Adjusters (Users)
* Customer Portal (React SPA / HTTPS / TLS 1.3)
* Adjuster Web Application (React SPA / OAuth2 / OIDC)
* Backend-For-Frontend (BFF) Container (Node.js / REST / HTTPS)
* Routing Container (Go / mTLS)
* Azure Service Bus (Messaging)
* Azure Blob Storage (Document & Photo Storage)
* Azure Active Directory / Entra ID (Identity Provider)
* Legacy COBOL/DB2 Mainframe (On-premises System of Record)
* ArgoCD (GitOps Deployment)

## Relationships
* Customers and Brokers -> Customer Portal: Submits claims, uploads documents, and tracks status [HTTPS/TLS 1.3]
* Customer Portal -> BFF Container: Communicates via REST APIs [HTTPS/TLS 1.3]
* Customer Portal -> Azure Blob Storage: Uploads evidence directly [HTTPS / SAS Tokens]
* BFF Container -> Routing Container: Forwards requests and handles latency [mTLS]
* Routing Container -> Legacy COBOL/DB2 Mainframe: Interfaces with legacy system [mTLS / Max 1 change/quarter]
* BFF Container -> Azure Service Bus: Publishes and consumes async messages [AMQP / TLS]
* Customer Portal & Adjuster App -> Azure Active Directory: Authenticates users [OAuth2 / OIDC]

## Technology Stack
* Frontend: React with Web Crypto API and strict Content Security Policy for secure stateless rendering and local encryption
* Backend & Routing: Node.js for BFF and Go for the Routing Container to ensure efficient performance and low latency
* Infrastructure & Deployment: Azure West Europe, Bicep templates for Infrastructure-as-Code, and ArgoCD for GitOps automated deployments
* Messaging & Storage: Azure Service Bus for reliable eventing and Azure Blob Storage with SAS tokens for secure direct uploads
* Security: Azure Active Directory (Entra ID) for Single Sign-On, TLS 1.3, and mTLS across hybrid boundaries

## Rationale
This architecture decouples the modern React frontend from the legacy mainframe via a Node.js BFF and Go Routing container, protecting the system from strict legacy interface constraints. Furthermore, direct-to-blob SAS uploads and stateless design patterns mitigate the team's low cloud experience while ensuring high performance, security, and a seamless 3-year migration path.

Adjuster Web Application.analysis:
## Overview
[Modern Claims Platform that gradually replaces a 30-year-old on-premises COBOL/DB2 mainframe claims system with a hybrid cloud architecture in Azure West Europe while ensuring zero downtime.]

## Key Elements
- Claims Adjusters (Primary internal users)
- Adjuster Web Application (React SPA container)
- Backend-For-Frontend (BFF) Container (Node.js)
- Azure Front Door with WAF (Edge routing and security)
- Azure Active Directory / Entra ID (Identity provider)
- Azure Monitor (Observability and audit logging)

## Relationships
- Claims Adjusters -> Adjuster Web Application: Manages claims via UI [HTTPS / TLS 1.3]
- Adjuster Web Application -> Azure Front Door: Accesses web interface [HTTPS]
- Azure Front Door -> BFF Container: Routes API requests and static assets [HTTPS]
- BFF Container -> Azure Active Directory / Entra ID: Authenticates and manages sessions [OAuth2/OIDC]
- BFF Container -> Azure Monitor: Ships audit logs and telemetry [HTTPS / OpenTelemetry]

## Technology Stack
- React: Powers the Adjuster Web Application for high-performance UI rendering
- Node.js: Implements the BFF container for secure session and token management
- Azure Front Door with WAF: Provides edge security, TLS termination, and DDoS protection
- Azure Active Directory (Entra ID): Manages single sign-on and RBAC authorization
- Azure Monitor: Handles distributed tracing and cryptographically verifiable audit logging

## Rationale
[This architecture securely separates frontend presentation from legacy backend complexity while leveraging managed Azure services to compensate for the team's limited cloud experience. Backend-driven session management and edge security protect sensitive PII and financial data without disrupting multi-tab adjuster workflows.]

• Azure Active Directory (Entra ID)
• Customer Portal (React / HTTPS)

Routing Container.analysis:
## Overview
[The system is a hybrid cloud Insurance Claims Modernization platform that gradually replaces a 30-year-old on-premises mainframe with a modern Azure-hosted solution while ensuring continuous business operations.]

## Key Elements
- Customers and Brokers
- Claims Adjusters
- IT Administrators
- Legacy System (COBOL/DB2 Mainframe)
- Azure Active Directory (Entra ID)
- Customer Portal (React / HTTPS)
- Adjuster Web Application (React / OAuth2 / OIDC)
- Backend-For-Frontend (BFF) Container (Node.js / REST / HTTPS)
- Routing Container (Go / mTLS)
- Azure Service Bus (Azure Messaging)
- ArgoCD (GitOps)

## Relationships
- Customer Portal -> BFF Container: Submits claims online [HTTPS]
- Adjuster Web Application -> BFF Container: Handles claims [HTTPS]
- BFF Container -> Azure Service Bus: Publishes claim events [AMQP]
- Routing Container -> COBOL/DB2 Mainframe: Routes claims traffic to legacy system [mTLS]
- Routing Container -> ArgoCD: Synchronizes routing tables via GitOps configuration pipeline [Git]

## Technology Stack
- Go: Chosen for the Routing Container for high-performance network handling and low memory footprint.
- mTLS: Enforces strict bidirectional TLS with certificate pinning for secure hybrid communication.
- Azure Key Vault: Secures private keys and certificates for hybrid bridging, preventing plain-text storage.
- OpenTelemetry: Mandated for distributed tracing across the Azure boundary and on-premises mainframe.
- ArgoCD: Manages GitOps-driven configuration for rapid 1-day claim type rollbacks.

## Rationale
[This hybrid architecture isolates expensive mainframe dependencies while gradually migrating claim types via a resilient Routing Container. It satisfies strict latency, consistency, and security requirements through modern cloud patterns and GitOps control.]

Azure Service Bus.analysis:
## Overview
The system is a hybrid Insurance Claims Modernization platform that gradually replaces a legacy COBOL/DB2 mainframe with a cloud-native Azure stack. Its core purpose is to decouple online claim submissions and adjuster workflows from the mainframe while guaranteeing zero message loss and seamless migration fallback.

## Key Elements
- **Azure Service Bus (Premium Tier):** Core messaging backbone handling asynchronous event publishing and queuing.
- **Backend-For-Frontend (BFF) Container (Node.js):** Message producer enforcing schema validation and envelope encryption.
- **Message Consumers (AKS):** Scaled via KEDA to process events asynchronously.
- **Azure Key Vault:** Manages Customer-Managed Keys (CMK) for encryption at rest.
- **ArgoCD & Terraform:** GitOps pipeline for infrastructure management.

## Relationships
- **BFF Container -> Azure Service Bus:** Publishes asynchronous claim events over AMQP with TLS 1.3 and Managed Identities (Azure RBAC).
- **Azure Service Bus -> Message Consumers:** Delivers queued events for downstream processing via secure Private Link endpoints.
- **Azure Service Bus -> Azure Key Vault:** Secures payload data at rest using Customer-Managed Keys.

## Technology Stack
- **Azure Service Bus Premium Tier:** Selected to support 14-day message retention, VNet integration, and partitioned throughput.
- **Azure Private Link & Private Endpoints:** Secures hybrid connectivity by bypassing the public internet entirely.
- **Azure RBAC & Managed Identities:** Replaces SAS keys to enforce least-privilege access control.
- **KEDA (Kubernetes Event-driven Autoscaling):** Scales processor pods dynamically based on queue depth (`MessagesActive`).

## Rationale
This architecture uses Azure Service Bus Premium with strict security, private networking, and idempotency controls to satisfy strict consistency (R-04) and security (R-07) requirements in a hybrid migration. It insulates the fragile on-premises mainframe from traffic spikes while safely handling operational retries and gradual claim-type migrations.

ArgoCD.analysis:
## Overview
[The system modernizes a 30-year-old regional insurance claims mainframe by gradually migrating claim types to a hybrid cloud platform. It ensures continuous claims processing, zero data loss, and rapid rollback capabilities.]

## Key Elements
- IT Administrators (Users)
- ArgoCD (GitOps Container)
- Azure Active Directory / Entra ID (External Authentication System)
- Routing Container (Go / mTLS)
- Azure Service Bus (Messaging Container)
- Azure Key Vault (Secret Management)
- Azure Monitor / SIEM (Observability)

## Relationships
- IT Administrators -> ArgoCD: Manages container rollouts and rollbacks via GitOps [HTTPS / Azure AD SSO]
- ArgoCD -> Azure Key Vault: Injects secrets securely at runtime [External Secrets Operator]
- ArgoCD -> Routing Container: Synchronizes routing configurations and feature flags [In-cluster API]
- ArgoCD -> Azure Monitor: Ships audit logs and application health metrics [HTTPS]

## Technology Stack
- ArgoCD: GitOps engine chosen to standardize rollouts and enable 1-day rollbacks for cloud-inexperienced teams.
- Azure Active Directory (Entra ID): Enforces SSO and RBAC for IT Administrator access.
- Azure Key Vault: Secures runtime secrets, preventing plain-text storage in Git.
- Azure Monitor: Collects audit logs and health metrics for operational visibility.

## Rationale
[This architecture uses declarative GitOps to simplify hybrid deployments and enable rapid rollbacks for a cloud-inexperienced team. It strictly separates deployment reconciliation from business logic, ensuring secure, compliant, and zero-downtime claim migrations.]
